title: SDK playbooks & starter templates for streaming + retry ergonomics across TS/Py/Go
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Create a set of production-ready starter templates and short cookbook snippets that demonstrate idiomatic usage of Redwood SDKs across TypeScript (Next.js Edge + API routes), Python (FastAPI async streaming + retry helpers), and Go (HTTP server with context cancellation + CLI). The deliverable is a small repository of examples + a playbook doc describing unified retry semantics, streaming backpressure handling, and copy-pasteable snippets for engineers.

Background: We repeatedly see support questions and onboarding friction for streaming APIs and retry behavior across languages. Differences in default retry semantics and stream ergonomics lead to inconsistent app behavior (e.g., duplicate outputs, lack of cancellation, or unbounded reconnect loops). This ticket bundles a set of starter templates and a short SDK playbook to promote consistent, secure, and cost-aware usage.

Scope:
- Next.js: two templates: Edge route example (Edge runtime streaming using Web Streams API) and serverless API route (Node fetch streaming with async iterator and AbortController).
- FastAPI: async generator streaming example with graceful cancellation via request background tasks and a small retry helper using tenacity patterns.
- Go: net/http example showing context propagation to RPC, streaming via chunked responses, and a CLI example that uses context cancellation and progress feedback.
- Cookbook snippets: small recipes for exponential backoff + jitter, idempotency token guidance, streaming reconnection policy, and token-level cost estimation tips for template authors.
- Playbook doc: one-page guidance for SDK maintainers and integrators mapping SDK primitives to a unified behavior (max_attempts, base_delay, jitter, idempotency, streaming_resume_token).

Acceptance criteria:
- PRs with working examples for all three language families merged to examples repo.
- Playbook.md in the repo with examples and an API compatibility table.
- CI checks that run linting and a smoke-test that the examples can start locally and stream at least 3 tokens.

Out of scope: full tutorial blog posts and sample apps that implement business logic. This ticket focuses on minimal, well-documented starter templates and the playbook.

Example CLI uses spinners and prints cumulative token counts. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/326

2026-03-10 — Maya Chen: Consolidated PRs and updated Playbook.md with unified retry params: max_attempts=3, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, jitter=full_jitter. Also included a table mapping SDK options to playbook params. Marking ticket for follow-up review next week.
notes: Key decisions and trade-offs: 1) Use full_jitter for backoff to avoid thundering herd. 2) Default to client-side idempotency tokens for non-streaming mutating requests; streaming responses are expected to be resumed using server-provided resume tokens when supported. 3) For Next.js Edge, prefer Web Streams and lightweight parsing on the client; for Node API routes, provide an AbortController example to abort long polls. 4) Keep examples minimal (<= 150 lines each) and heavily commented for copy-paste onboarding.
how_to_test: 1) Clone examples repo and run `./scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh`. 2) For Next.js Edge: `vercel dev` then curl the edge route and assert at least 3 chunked tokens. 3) FastAPI: `uvicorn examples.fastapi:app --reload` and hit /stream; verify process exits cleanly on Ctrl+C. 4) Go CLI: build and run `examples-go cli --prompt 'hello'` and observe spinner and token counters. CI will run these steps automatically in a container.
